items.explanation: Unrestricted U-boat warfare, the Lusitania sinking, and the Zimmermann Telegram all pushed America toward war — but the 1916 Sussex Pledge was Germany promising restraint, the one step away from war.
options: A. The Sussex Pledge
B. Germany's 1917 U-boat campaign
C. The sinking of the Lusitania
D. The Zimmermann Telegram
items.stem: All of the following moved America toward war with Germany EXCEPT

items.explanation: Wilson dreamed of a democratic peace, but Clemenceau's France wanted Germany crippled — reparations, territory, and security — clashing fundamentally with the Fourteen Points.
options: A. They opposed any League of Nations
B. They resented Germany's exclusion from peacemaking
C. They disdained Wilson personally
D. They wanted to punish Germany, not reform the world
items.stem: France opposed much of Wilson's Fourteen Points because

items.explanation: The home front mobilized through Liberty Bond drives — with stars like Chaplin and Fairbanks headlining rallies — plus the draft, war industries, and propaganda. There were no ration cards or German-American camps.
options: A. Ration cards went to every family
B. German-Americans were herded into camps
C. Cities drilled for enemy attack
D. Celebrities helped sell Liberty Bonds

items.explanation: Critics noted the Lusitania carried munitions (making it a legal target), that Germany had sunk liners before, and that Berlin had advertised warnings in U.S. papers — all three arguments circulated.
options: A. The ship carried contraband munitions
B. Germany had sunk passenger ships before
C. Germany had published warnings in American papers
D. All of the above
items.stem: Critics who said America had no right to outrage over the Lusitania argued

items.explanation: Senators feared Article X would let the League commit American troops without Congress — surrendering the constitutional war power.
options: A. The U.S. would have to bankroll the League
B. The League could commit U.S. troops without Congress
C. The public unanimously opposed membership
D. Germany and Russia would dominate the League
items.stem: Many senators opposed joining the League of Nations because

items.explanation: America emerged as the world's creditor and a power broker at Versailles — its international weight vastly increased even as it rejected the League.
options: A. America's international influence grew
B. America's international influence shrank
C. America conquered new imperial territories
D. America lost its overseas possessions
items.stem: Which was a significant result of World War I?
items.stimulus:
Questions 6–8 refer to the following excerpt.

"You may call me selfish if you will, conservative or reactionary, or use any other harsh adjective you see fit to apply, but an American I was born, an American I have remained all my life. I can never be anything else."
—Senator Henry Cabot Lodge, 1919 (abridged)

items.explanation: Wilson sold the League as the machine that would keep the peace — collective security replacing the old alliance systems that had failed.
options: A. Rebuild war-devastated territories
B. Aid new nations freed from colonial rule
C. Guarantee postwar stability and security
D. Restore the prewar alliance systems
